question: Should OpenClaw add opt-in per-message timestamps to the core TUI, and should the control be persisted config, an in-session toggle, or both?
rationale: The source-visible gap is clear, but the requested solution changes user-facing TUI behavior and may add config/default surface, so automation should not choose the permanent UX contract alone.

options.title: Approve opt-in TUI timestamps
options.body: Allow a narrow implementation that keeps timestamps disabled by default, reuses persisted message timestamps when available, and proves live plus replayed rows in the TUI PTY lane.

options.title: Prefer session-only toggle
options.body: Avoid growing persisted config and accept only a lightweight in-session TUI command or settings control if maintainers want a smaller surface.

options.title: Decline core support
options.body: Keep the TUI visually minimal and leave timing inspection to logs, transcript data, or a future broader transcript view.

recommendation.title: Approve opt-in TUI timestamps
recommendation.body: Allow a narrow implementation that keeps timestamps disabled by default, reuses persisted message timestamps when available, and proves live plus replayed rows in the TUI PTY lane.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current evidence ties vincentkoc to recent ChatLog and timestamp-reconciliation maintenance on the affected path.
